 GameSim is a game development studio that partners with clients to build games across PC/console and a range of art styles. We care about craftsmanship, collaboration, and shipping work we’re proud to put our names on. If you love building environments and believable spaces we’d like to meet you. Our headquarters is based in Orlando, FL!
 Talent Pipeline Posting Notice 
Please note that this posting is not tied to an immediate vacancy. We are proactively building a pipeline of qualified candidates in anticipation of potential hiring needs over the coming months. Applications will be reviewed and retained for future consideration as opportunities arise.
 We are seeking a Lighting Artist to create high-quality real-time lighting and help support the execution of lighting work across GameSim projects.
 This is a hands-on production role with opportunities to take on project-level leadership responsibilities. In addition to completing assigned lighting work, you may help coordinate tasks, review the work of other artists, provide constructive feedback, and ensure scenes meet the visual and technical quality bar established by Art Direction and the client.
 You will collaborate with Art Directors, Environment Artists, Technical Artists, VFX Artists, Designers, Engineers, Producers, clients, and partner studios to translate creative direction into lighting solutions that support mood, gameplay readability, environmental storytelling, and performance.
 What Success Looks Like
 Within your first 90 days, you will:
 Develop a clear understanding of the project’s visual direction, lighting pipeline, gameplay requirements, technical constraints, and production schedule.
 Build effective working relationships with Art Direction, Production, Technical Art, Environment Art, Design, and other project disciplines.
 Create polished lighting work that meets the project’s established visual and technical quality bar.
 Take ownership of lighting for assigned scenes, environments, sequences, or gameplay areas.
 Provide useful feedback and support to other artists when asked to review or coordinate lighting work.
 Identify artistic, technical, or production risks early and communicate them to the appropriate project leads.
 Deliver assigned work on schedule and respond effectively to internal and client feedback.
 Responsibilities
 Lighting Creation and Execution
 Create high-quality real-time lighting for gameplay environments, levels, cinematics, characters, and interactive sequences.
 Translate art direction, concept art, reference material, gameplay requirements, narrative goals, and client feedback into effective lighting solutions.
 Use lighting to establish mood, atmosphere, visual hierarchy, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Ensure lighting supports gameplay readability, navigation, combat visibility, character presentation, and important interactive elements.
 Develop and refine exposure, color, contrast, fog, atmosphere, reflections, shadows, emissive response, color grading, and post-processing.
 Create lighting for a range of visual styles, including realistic, stylized, cinematic, and highly art-directed projects.
 Maintain visual consistency across related environments, gameplay spaces, sequences, times of day, and lighting conditions.
 Bring assigned scenes from initial lighting setup through final polish.
 Respond to feedback from Art Direction, project leadership, and clients in a timely and professional manner.
 Ensure completed work meets project requirements for quality, performance, organization, and delivery.
 Leadership and Quality Support
 Help oversee lighting work for an assigned scene, group of scenes, feature, or milestone when requested by project leadership.
 Review the work of other lighting artists or multidisciplinary artists contributing to lighting.
 Provide clear, respectful, and actionable feedback through written notes, live reviews, reference images, paintovers, or in-engine examples.
 Help ensure lighting work follows approved visual targets, technical standards, and project requirements.
 Communicate expected outcomes, priorities, and quality standards to artists working within an assigned area.
 Monitor the visual progress of assigned lighting work and identify scenes that may require additional revision or support.
 Confirm that feedback has been addressed before work is submitted for senior, Art Director, or client review.
 Support junior or less-experienced artists with lighting fundamentals, engine workflows, scene organization, optimization, and production practices.
 Lead by example through reliable execution, clear communication, constructive collaboration, and professional conduct.
 Escalate unresolved quality, schedule, scope, or technical concerns to the appropriate senior artist, Art Director, or Producer.
 Planning and Production Support
 Work with Art Direction and Production to understand lighting priorities, tasks, estimates, and milestone expectations.
 Help break lighting goals into clear and manageable production tasks.
 Provide progress updates and communicate when assigned work is at risk of missing quality, technical, or scheduling requirements.
 Participate in daily reviews, art reviews, milestone evaluations, and planning discussions.
 Help prepare lighting work for internal reviews, client presentations, milestone submissions, and final delivery.
 Balance hands-on production responsibilities with review, coordination, troubleshooting, and team support.
 Adjust priorities when creative direction, technical requirements, production scope, or client feedback changes.
 Maintain accurate task status and documentation using the project’s production-management tools.
 Technical and Pipeline Responsibilities
 Work with Technical Art and Engineering to ensure lighting is visually effective, technically stable, and appropriate for the target platform.
 Follow established budgets for dynamic lights, shadows, volumetrics, reflections, global illumination, memory, and scalability.
 Identify and help resolve issues involving exposure, shadow artifacts, light leaking, reflections, volumetrics, bake quality, material response, and post-processing.
 Use dynamic, baked, stationary, or hybrid lighting approaches according to the project’s established pipeline.
 Profile assigned lighting work and make informed visual adjustments to meet performance requirements.
 Validate lighting across relevant gameplay cameras, display settings, hardware targets, times of day, weather states, and scalability levels.
 Follow project standards for scene organization, naming conventions, source control, documentation, and asset integration.
 Contribute to reusable lighting setups, templates, documentation, validation processes, and team best practices.
 Identify workflow problems and communicate potential improvements to senior artists, Technical Art, or project leadership.
 Cross-Discipline Collaboration
 Collaborate with Environment Art to ensure geometry, materials, composition, and set dressing support the intended lighting.
 Partner with VFX to integrate fog, particles, weather, fire, emissive effects, and atmospheric elements.
 Work with Design to ensure lighting supports navigation, player guidance, combat readability, objectives, and interactive systems.
 Coordinate with Character Art and Animation to maintain readable and appealing character presentation.
 Support cinematic lighting needs involving shot composition, continuity, exposure, character lighting, and narrative focus.
 Communicate artistic and technical concerns clearly to both creative and non-creative stakeholders.
 Work effectively with distributed teams, partner studios, external vendors, and clients across different time zones.
 Requirements
 Professional experience creating lighting for games, real-time projects, animation, visualization, or a closely related field.
 A portfolio or reel demonstrating strong real-time lighting work.
 Strong understanding of lighting fundamentals, including value, color, contrast, composition, visual hierarchy, atmosphere, exposure, shadow, and material response.
 Experience lighting gameplay environments or interactive real-time scenes.
 Understanding of how lighting supports mood, gameplay readability, navigation, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Professional experience using Unreal Engine or another modern real-time engine.
 Experience with dynamic or baked lighting, global illumination, reflections, volumetrics, exposure, color grading, and post-processing.
 Working knowledge of physically based rendering and material response.
 Understanding of basic lighting optimization, including light cost, shadows, volumetrics, reflections, scalability, and platform constraints.
 Ability to take ownership of assigned scenes and follow them through review and completion.
 Ability to receive, interpret, and implement artistic and technical feedback.
 Experience reviewing artwork or providing constructive feedback to teammates.
 Ability to identify work that does not meet an established quality target and communicate practical improvements.
 Ability to balance visual quality, technical requirements, production scope, and schedule.
 Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
 Ability to organize priorities, communicate risks, and follow work through to completion.
 Experience collaborating with multiple game-development disciplines.
 Ability to adapt to different projects, visual styles, engines, pipelines, platforms, and client expectations.
 Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a distributed team.
 Tools and Technical Experience
 Candidates should have experience with a professional real-time lighting toolset. This may include:
 Unreal Engine 5 or another modern real-time engine
 Lumen or comparable real-time global-illumination systems
 GPU Lightmass, CPU Lightmass, or comparable baked-lighting systems
 Real-time profiling, visualization, and debugging tools
 Photoshop or comparable image-editing software
 DaVinci Resolve, Nuke, After Effects, or comparable color and compositing tools
 Maya, Blender, 3ds Max, or another 3D content-creation package
 Perforce or another production source-control system
 Jira, Confluence, Miro, or comparable planning and documentation tools
 Expertise with every listed application is not required. We are primarily interested in candidates who demonstrate strong lighting fundamentals, sound production judgment, adaptability, and the ability to learn project-specific tools.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience working in co-development, outsourcing, consulting, or work-for-hire game production.
 Experience contributing to a shipped PC or console title.
 Experience working across realistic and stylized visual pipelines.
 Previous experience acting as a lighting point person, task coordinator, reviewer, or feature owner.
 Experience guiding junior artists or supporting teammates without formal management authority.
 Experience working with remote teams, partner studios, or external vendors.
 Experience owning lighting for a level, environment, sequence, or gameplay feature.
 Knowledge of Unreal Engine systems such as Lumen, Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps, volumetric fog, reflection systems, exposure controls, post-process volumes, and scalability settings.
 Experience with dynamic time-of-day systems, weather systems, destructible environments, or changing gameplay states.
 Experience lighting cinematics, characters, dialogue scenes, or scripted sequences.
 Knowledge of cinematography, photography, film lighting, camera exposure, and color theory.
 Familiarity with HDR displays, tone mapping, calibration, or accessibility considerations.
 Familiarity with rendering pipelines, shader behavior, and material development.
 Familiarity with Blueprints, Python, editor scripting, automation, or technical-art workflows.
 Experience creating lighting documentation, templates, benchmark scenes, or review materials.
 Portfolio Requirements
 Your portfolio or reel should demonstrate:
 Strong real-time lighting with effective composition, mood, color, contrast, readability, atmosphere, and scene cohesion.
 Work presented in a commercial, proprietary, or modern real-time engine.
 Clear explanations of your individual contribution, responsibilities, workflow, and production decisions.
 Gameplay lighting that guides attention, supports navigation, and reinforces the intended player experience.
 Effective integration between lighting, environments, materials, VFX, atmosphere, characters, and post-processing.
 An understanding of optimization, scalability, technical limitations, and production constraints.
 Examples showing ownership of lighting from initial setup through final delivery.
 The ability to work from concept art, reference, environment blockouts, narrative direction, gameplay requirements, or developing creative direction.
 Adaptability across different projects, genres, visual styles, or lighting conditions.
 We also encourage applicants to include:
 Day and night treatments of the same environment.
 Dynamic and baked lighting examples.
 Lighting created for different gameplay states, weather conditions, or times of day.
 Before-and-after comparisons showing how lighting improved readability, mood, composition, or performance.
 Examples of work reviewed or coordinated under your guidance, with your responsibilities clearly explained.
 Lighting guides, reference boards, benchmark scenes, review notes, documentation, or templates created for teammates.
 Please clearly identify your individual contribution to collaborative work.

Who We Are 
 SWTCH is pioneering EV charging solutions for multifamily and commercial properties across North America. Since 2016, our team of entrepreneurs, energy professionals, and technologists has been focused on unlocking the social, economic, and environmental benefits of widespread EV adoption. Today, our solutions are deployed in tens of thousands of locations —many of which are low-to-moderate income housing—helping to make clean mobility accessible for all.
 With an expanding footprint across Canada and the U.S., we’re scaling quickly and looking for mission-driven talent to help accelerate our growth.
 Job Opportunity 
 At SWTCH, we're on a mission to make electric vehicle (EV) charging accessible, reliable, and intelligent for everyone. As a bilingual Customer Success Manager (CSM) , you'll play a critical role in helping our customers get the full value of SWTCH's EV charging and energy management platform. Those customers include real estate owners, utilities, municipalities, and enterprise partners. You'll manage a dedicated portfolio of named accounts and also help support a pooled book of shared customers. That means balancing high-touch relationship management with scalable, program-driven engagement, so every SWTCH customer gets a consistent, high-quality experience.
 You'll drive value realization, customer adoption, and account health across the customer journey, for both your assigned and shared accounts. As a trusted advisor, you'll align customer goals with SWTCH's solutions and work with teams across the company, and with your fellow CSMs, to deliver a seamless experience. This role is ideal for a proactive, organized communicator who enjoys building relationships and solving problems, works well in a team, and wants to help customers make the transition to electric mobility.
 What You’ll Be Doing
 Relationship Management : Build and maintain strong, long-term relationships with a portfolio of customers across the real estate, multifamily, and commercial sectors. Also support a pooled book of shared accounts alongside the broader Customer Success team.
 Hybrid Coverage Model: Own day-to-day success for named accounts while taking requests, escalations, and engagement tasks from the pooled account queue. Keep a consistent, high-quality experience for every customer, whether or not they have a dedicated CSM.
 Scaled Engagement: Run one-to-many programs for pooled accounts, such as webinars, email campaigns, office hours, and self-serve resources, to drive adoption and engagement efficiently.
 Onboarding & Implementation: Lead the onboarding process for new assigned customers, ensuring smooth transitions from sale to active charging operations through milestone tracking and stakeholder alignment.
 Customer Advocacy: Act as the "voice of the customer" internally, working with Product, Operations, and Support to resolve issues and influence the product roadmap. Surface trends that affect the wider customer base as well as individual accounts.
 Value Realization: Hold regular check-ins and business reviews with assigned accounts, and deliver scalable value touchpoints to pooled accounts. Communicate impact, share usage insights, and help customers meet their sustainability and ROI goals.
 Retention & Growth: Manage contract renewals and identify opportunities for account expansion, such as adding new charging stations or upgrading software features.
 Health Monitoring: Track customer health metrics and adoption trends to proactively identify at-risk accounts and mitigate churn.
 Documentation & Collaboration: Keep account notes, activity logs, and next steps clear and up to date in the CRM, so any team member can pick up a pooled account smoothly and handoffs work well.
 Process Improvement: Help build Customer Success playbooks, pooled-account workflows, and resources that let us scale our operations as we grow.
 Technical Liaison: Partner with our technical and support teams to help troubleshoot site-level issues and ensure customers understand how to use SWTCH’s reporting and management tools.
 You Have
 3+ years in Customer Success, Account Management, or a similar client-facing role, preferably within SaaS, Cleantech, or Real Estate.
 Bilingual Fluency in English and French is strongly preferred.
 Strong Communication: Excellent verbal and written skills, with the ability to explain platform features to both non-technical owners and site managers.
 Problem-Solving Skills: A proactive mindset with the ability to navigate challenges and find creative solutions for customers.
 Data Literacy: Comfortable using data to tell a story; experience with Excel and CRM tools (e.g., Salesforce, ChurnZero, Zendesk) to track customer progress.

 Passion for Sustainability: A genuine interest in the EV industry and helping transition the world to a cleaner energy future.
 Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Communications, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
 Bonus Points 
 Experience with connected hardware systems (EV chargers, IoT, telecom gear, BMS, gateways, etc).
 Familiarity with networking fundamentals (IP addressing, LTE/cellular connectivity, firewalls, etc).
 Understanding of OCPP, load management, or similar protocols (or willingness to learn quickly).

About the Role
We are looking for experienced Senior Autonomous Vehicle Technicians to support the maintenance, diagnostics, repair, and operational readiness of autonomous vehicle fleets and robotaxi operations across North America.
As a Senior Autonomous Vehicle Technician, you will be responsible for ensuring that electric and autonomous vehicles remain safe, reliable, and ready for daily deployment. This role supports autonomous ride-hailing services, robotaxi fleet operations, on-road testing programs, and new city launches where vehicle uptime, technical precision, and safety compliance are critical.
You will work closely with AV Operations Leads, Depot Specialists, Safety Operators, SDS Specialists, engineering teams, and fleet operations teams to minimize vehicle downtime and keep the fleet operational. The role combines hands-on automotive repair, EV diagnostics, high-voltage safety, software updates, and support for autonomous driving hardware.
This position is ideal for an experienced automotive technician who wants to move into the future of mobility and work directly with electric vehicles, autonomous driving systems, ADAS technology, robotics, and self-driving vehicle platforms.

Key Responsibilities: Autonomous Vehicle Maintenance 
 Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on electric and autonomous vehicles used in robotaxi fleet operations .
 Ensure vehicles are technically ready for daily deployment, testing, commercial operations, and autonomous ride-hailing services .
 Conduct detailed vehicle inspections to support fleet readiness , vehicle uptime, and operational safety.
 Diagnose and repair mechanical, electrical, electronic, and software-related vehicle issues.
 Support maintenance workflows for high-availability autonomous vehicle fleets operating in shift-based or 24/7 environments.
 Advanced Diagnostics & Repair 
 Perform advanced diagnostics on EV platforms, ADAS systems, autonomous driving hardware, and vehicle electronic systems.
 Use OEM diagnostic tools, service software, and technical procedures to identify root causes of vehicle faults.
 Troubleshoot issues related to battery systems, drivetrains, braking systems, steering systems, sensors, cameras, wiring, and vehicle control modules.
 Replace, repair, and validate vehicle components according to safety, quality, and technical standards.
 Escalate complex technical issues to engineering teams with clear documentation and diagnostic findings.
 EV & High-Voltage Systems 
 Work safely with electric vehicle systems , including high-voltage batteries, charging systems, inverters, and electric drivetrains.
 Follow strict high-voltage safety procedures when performing diagnostics, repairs, and component replacements.
 Support charging readiness and EV fleet availability in coordination with depot operations.
 Identify risks related to EV systems and escalate safety concerns immediately.
 Autonomous Driving Hardware Support 
 Support installation, inspection, and replacement of autonomous vehicle hardware components.
 Assist with checks related to cameras, LiDAR, radar, compute units, wiring harnesses, sensor mounts, and related vehicle systems.
 Coordinate with SDS Specialists when issues involve the self-driving system , sensor calibration, or autonomous driving software.
 Ensure autonomous driving hardware remains properly installed, clean, functional, and ready for operation.
 Software Updates & Technical Validation 
 Perform vehicle software updates, configuration changes, and validation checks according to defined procedures.
 Support post-repair testing to confirm vehicle functionality before returning the vehicle to robotaxi operations .
 Verify that repairs and maintenance actions do not impact vehicle safety, operational readiness, or autonomous system performance.
 Maintain accurate service records, diagnostic reports, and repair documentation.

 Votre profil

 Gérer l’ensemble du cycle de vie après-vente des comptes stratégiques : intégration, adoption, renouvellement et expansion.

 Créer et maintenir du contenu spécifique à Devs.ai pour la base de connaissances et le centre de soutien.

 Recevoir les retours clients en lien avec le produit et être le porte-parole des clients auprès de l'équipe produit.
 Assurer la liaison entre les clients et nos équipes responsables des produits et de l’ingénierie, en traduisant les retours en informations concrètes.

 Expérience à gérer des comptes stratégiques avec un accompagnement personnalisé.

 An overview of this role 
 As a Senior Revenue Operations Manager at GitLab, you'll own work the whole go-to-market organization relies on: the policies and processes that govern how we sell and book deals, our global forecasting process, and the Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) operating cadence. You'll report to the Senior Manager, Sales Operations, and work closely with sales leadership, other Revenue Strategy & Operations teams, Finance, Deal Desk, Product, and Data.
 This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll bring experience running a forecast process day to day and a practical understanding of how a sales organization works. You'll work independently to take a problem from "something looks off in the numbers" to a fix that sticks.
 GitLab is all-remote, and most of our work happens in writing. Clear, concise documentation is a big part of this job.
 What you’ll do 
 Own the policies that define how deals are booked, credited, and forecasted, including bookings rules, opportunity netting, and sales stages and exit criteria. Write them, get them approved, and make sure the field understands what changed and why.
 Identify process problems before they affect the numbers. Validate and size the problem with data, find the root cause, and drive the fix with the right team, whether that's Revenue Systems, Deal Desk, Enablement, or compensation.
 Partner with Revenue Systems to build policy into system rules, validations, and alerts, reducing manual reviews and after-the-fact corrections.
 Improve forecast methodology by tracking actual results against the forecast, explaining variances, and changing processes that aren't working. Partner with Finance and Revenue Analytics to reconcile the field forecast with the finance outlook.
 Own the weekly forecast readout for the CRO and sales leadership, keeping it short and focused on decisions. Bring the forecasting and policy perspective into annual planning.
 Coordinate the CRO organization's weekly, monthly, and quarterly reviews, metrics, and follow-ups. Measure their impact on pipeline hygiene, data quality, forecast accuracy, and bookings, and change the cadence where it isn't working.
 Work with other Revenue Strategy & Operations teams, Finance, Product, Data, and Enablement to deliver changes from the first draft through field adoption. Keep cadence documentation current so the organization knows what happens when, who owns it, and what's expected.
 Mentor others on the team and improve how we document and run our processes.
 What you’ll bring 
 Experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, management consulting, or a similar role, including running a forecast process day to day in a business-to-business (B2B) subscription business.
 A practical understanding of how a sales organization runs, including pipeline stages, deal bookings and crediting, bookings and annual recurring revenue (ARR) definitions, and how compensation influences sales representative behavior.
 Strong data and analysis skills. You're highly proficient in Excel or Google Sheets, can build a model from scratch, and check your own numbers before sharing them.
 The ability to work independently, identify what needs to be done, and work with stakeholders to get it done. You involve your manager when you need a decision or hit a blocker.
 Clear, concise writing. You can turn a complex issue into a short document or Slack message that a senior leader will read and act on.
 Comfort working with senior leaders, including taking feedback from a CRO and turning it into a better process or a more useful readout.
 Systems thinking and the ability to learn new tools and domains quickly. You understand how customer relationship management (CRM), quoting, billing, and compensation systems connect, and how a change in one affects the others. How you think matters more to us than which forecasting tool you've used.
 Helpful, but not required: experience rolling out bookings, crediting, or deal policies; forecasting consumption or usage-based revenue; using tools such as Clari and Salesforce reporting; or a consulting, strategy, or structured problem-solving background.
 About the team 
 The Sales Strategy & Operations team sits within Revenue Strategy & Operations at GitLab. We're a small team working closely with Finance, Deal Desk, Revenue Systems, Revenue Analytics, and sales leadership. We work asynchronously first, keep our documents short, and focus on practical solutions that make the field's job easier.

 Abbott est un chef de file mondial de l’industrie des soins de santé qui crée des solutions scientifiques révolutionnaires visant à améliorer la santé des gens. L’entreprise est résolument tournée vers l’avenir, à l’affût des changements qui pourraient survenir dans le domaine des sciences et des technologies médicales.

 En étant à l’emploi d’Abbott, vous pourrez faire un travail qui compte, vous perfectionner et apprendre, prendre soin de vous et des membres de votre famille, rester fidèle à ce que vous êtes et vivre pleinement. Vous pourrez :
 profiter de possibilités d’avancement professionnel au sein d’une entreprise internationale qui vous permettra de bâtir la carrière dont vous rêvez;
 travailler pour une entreprise reconnue dans des douzaines de pays partout dans le monde comme étant un excellent milieu de travail et figurant parmi les entreprises les plus admirées dans le monde dans le classement Fortune;
 travailler pour une grande entreprise reconnue comme étant l’une des meilleures où travailler, notamment pour ce qui a trait à la diversité du personnel, à la conciliation travail-famille ainsi qu’à la place des femmes dans les postes de cadres et les postes scientifiques.
 L’occasion à saisir 
 Le Chef, Relations avec les parties prenantes travaillera pour Abbott Soins du diabète.  
 Ce que vous ferez  
 La personne titulaire du poste de chef des Relations avec les parties prenantes (Québec et Canada atlantique) est chargée d’établir et d’entretenir des relations stratégiques avec les principales parties prenantes externes au Québec, au Nouveau-Brunswick, en Nouvelle-Écosse, à l’Île-du-Prince-Édouard et à Terre-Neuve-et-Labrador. Cela comprend des interactions avec les représentants des gouvernements provinciaux (tant politiques qu’administratifs), les ministères de la Santé, les organismes chargés de l’évaluation des technologies de la santé et de l’élaboration des politiques, les professionnels de la santé, les leaders d’opinion clés, les groupes de défense des intérêts des patients ainsi que les associations professionnelles du secteur. Ce poste vise principalement à favoriser la réalisation des objectifs de l’entreprise en matière d’accès au marché, de politiques et d’affaires, grâce à une démarche proactive de défense des intérêts des parties prenantes. Le ou la chef dirige l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de stratégies régionales auprès des parties prenantes, repère les occasions d’influencer les décisions en matière de politiques et de financement, et établit des partenariats qui favorisent l’accès des patients à des solutions de soins de santé innovantes. De plus, la personne titulaire du poste fournit en temps opportun des renseignements et des analyses stratégiques à la direction, élabore des présentations et des documents d’information de grande qualité, et répond avec célérité aux besoins des parties prenantes et aux enjeux émergents afin d’assurer l’alignement avec les priorités de l’entreprise au Québec et dans le Canada atlantique.
 Stratégie d’accès au marché et mise en œuvre 
 Soutenir l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de stratégies provinciales d’accès au marché afin de faire progresser les objectifs de remboursement, de financement et d’accès des patients pour la gamme de produits d’Abbott Soins du diabète au Québec et dans le Canada atlantique.
 Évaluer les tendances, les priorités en matière de financement et les parcours d’accès des systèmes de santé provinciaux afin de cerner les occasions et les risques ayant une incidence sur l’accès aux technologies et aux solutions d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Interactions avec les parties prenantes – Accès au marché 
 Établir et entretenir des relations stratégiques avec les principales parties prenantes au Québec et dans le Canada atlantique, notamment les payeurs publics et privés, les professionnels de la santé, les leaders d’opinion clés, les décideurs des systèmes de santé, les parties prenantes de l’évaluation des technologies de la santé, les groupes de défense des intérêts des patients, les associations sectorielles et les représentants gouvernementaux.
 Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des plans de mobilisation des parties prenantes favorisant le financement, le remboursement et l’adoption de technologies et de solutions d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Représenter Abbott Soins du diabète dans les interactions avec les parties prenantes et tirer parti de leurs perspectives pour orienter les stratégies d’accès au marché, la planification commerciale et les priorités en matière d’accès.
 Soutien à l’évaluation des technologies de la santé et au remboursement 
 Appuyer les initiatives liées à l’évaluation des technologies de la santé, au remboursement et au financement concernant de la gamme de produits d’Abbotts Soins du diabète grâce à des renseignements sur les parties prenantes, à des analyses du contexte et à des perspectives stratégiques.
 Surveiller et évaluer les facteurs qui influencent les décisions en matière de remboursement, de liste des médicaments et de financement, et formuler des recommandations visant à optimiser l’accès des patients aux technologies d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Défense des intérêts des patients et partenariats avec les systèmes de santé 
 Établir et entretenir des partenariats avec des associations de patients et des parties prenantes du secteur de la santé afin de soutenir des initiatives visant à améliorer les résultats pour les personnes vivant avec le diabète et à élargir l’accès aux solutions d’Abbott Soins du diabète.
 Cerner les occasions de mener des actions collaboratives de défense des intérêts et de mettre en œuvre des initiatives liées aux systèmes de santé qui correspondent aux priorités des patients, des payeurs et des systèmes de santé.

 Fournir en temps opportun des analyses portant sur les changements de politiques, les points de vue des parties prenantes, les activités de la concurrence et les nouvelles tendances en matière d’accès, afin d’appuyer la prise de décisions stratégiques.
 Collaboration interfonctionnelle

 Develop computer vision and VLM approaches for scene understanding, object detection and tracking, activity recognition, and understanding events across video.

About Flosum 
Every large company now runs critical parts of its business on Salesforce: sales, service, financial data, patient records, citizen services. When a release breaks something or data goes missing, revenue stops and regulators call. Flosum is the platform these companies trust to ship changes safely, protect their data, and recover fast.
We are in the middle of the most exciting chapter in our history. Our customers have relied on our Salesforce-native platform for years. Now we are bringing them a new cloud-native platform they can run on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or on-premises. We have also launched sandbox management built for the AI era, so teams can test AI agents such as Agentforce on production-ready environments in minutes instead of days.
Our customers include some of the most demanding enterprises in banking, insurance, healthcare, the public sector, and technology. They don’t buy us casually, and they don’t leave us casually. Your job is to make sure they never want to.
 The role 
You will own a book of enterprise accounts and one number: retained revenue. You decide which accounts need you most this week, and you go there. This is a commercial role. You will spend your time with executives, not running support tickets.

 Own renewals across your book, from strategic accounts to smaller ones, and protect every dollar of recurring revenue.
 Build relationships with the executives who decide: CIOs, CTOs, VPs of Engineering, and heads of Salesforce platforms. Reach past your champion when the account needs it.

 Move customers from our Salesforce-native products to our cloud-native platform, and make the business case for why it matters to them.
 Defend your accounts against competitors, in-house builds, and new enterprise architectures.
 Pull the right people in. Hold product, support, engineering, and customer success accountable for what your customers need.
 Find expansion opportunities and hand them to our sales team with a clear plan.
 Run your book with discipline: accurate forecasts, clean renewal pipeline in Salesforce, no surprises.

 Commercial intensity. You negotiate well, you push for multi-year terms, and you are comfortable with hard conversations about price and value.

 Clear, concise writing and speaking. You can brief a CIO in five minutes.
 Experience in the Salesforce ecosystem is a strong plus.

 You will work with customers at the moment they move to the cloud. Few account managers get to shape a transition this large.

Why this role?

The Data Infrastructure team at Cohere is responsible for the storage and data movement layer underlying every model training run. We're building the unified storage layer that feeds our training workloads. It needs to serve petabytes of training data and model checkpoints fast enough to keep thousands of GPUs busy across several training clusters. In this role, you’d have an opportunity to build this system from the ground up. You’d be a key contributor, working on a problem few teams have had to solve at this scale.


In this role, you will:

 - Design, build, and operate the distributed storage system that feeds model training and evaluation.

 - Run this system multiple on Kubernetes clusters at petabyte scale.

 - Work with researchers and training-infra teams on how jobs actually read and write data, and turn that into throughput, latency, and durability requirements

 - Work through the networking, I/O, and consistency problems of moving large datasets and checkpoints across regions and backends, with GPU idle time and time-to-insight as the measures of success
   

You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Strong storage fundamentals, including replication, consistency, caching, and data lifecycle management.

 - Strong coding ability. We work in Python and Go; experience in either is enough, but you should be willing to pick up the other

 - Experience running stateful systems on Kubernetes, including Persistent Volumes, CSI drivers, and StatefulSets.

 - Hands-on experience with cloud object storage such as S3 as well as POSIX-style filesystems.
   

It’s a bonus if you have:

 - Experience with parallel or HPC filesystems such as Weka, VAST, or Lustre.

 - Familiarity with the data-loading and checkpointing patterns used in large-scale model training.

 - An interest in how large models are trained and evaluated, including the trajectory and eval data those runs generate, and a desire to understand the workloads the platform is serving.
